blocks.content:
High Court judges are removed in the same manner as Supreme Court judges.

Grounds:
• Proven misbehavior
• Incapacity

Procedure:
• Impeachment by Parliament with special majority.
High Court judges are removed in the same manner as Supreme Court judges.

items: High Court judges are NOT removed by the State Legislature; removal is carried out by Parliament.
The only two constitutional grounds for impeachment are 'Proven misbehavior' and 'Incapacity'.
Removal requires a special majority in Parliament, not a simple majority.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: High Court judges share the exact same removal procedure as Supreme Court judges.
The constitutional grounds for removal are strictly limited to proven misbehavior and incapacity.
The removal procedure requires an impeachment motion passed by Parliament.
The impeachment motion must be supported by a special majority in Parliament.
